anomalies.observed: Both CAN transceivers' primary-side GND1 and bus-side GND2 pins are connected to the same GND net.
anomalies.expected: For the specified isolated CAN interfaces, the transceivers' GND1 and GND2 domains should remain galvanically separated, with an isolated supply for the bus side as required.
anomalies.impact: The common-ground connection bypasses the transceivers' isolation barrier, so the CAN interfaces do not provide the specified galvanic isolation.

anomalies.observed: The two DIP-switch poles connect SW6.1–2 and SW6.3–4. R34.1 is on /CAN0_N and R34.2 on SW6.1; R35.1 is on /CAN1_N and R35.2 on SW6.2; SW6.3 and SW6.4 are on /CAN1_P and /CAN0_P, respectively. Closing the poles therefore joins the two positive CAN nets with one pole and joins the resistor ends across the negative nets with the other.
anomalies.expected: If these 120-ohm resistors and the DIP switch provide selectable CAN termination, each switch pole should place its resistor across the matching CAN pair, without joining CAN0 and CAN1.
anomalies.impact: Using the switch can couple the two CAN buses instead of independently terminating them, risking bus communication faults.

parsed.summary: The netlist defeats the specified CAN isolation by tying both sides of each transceiver to GND. It also shows the CAN termination switch wiring can couple CAN0 and CAN1 rather than terminate each bus independently.
